trust_boundaries.name: Attacker-influenceable telemetry into the agent's context

threats.summary: Instruction-like text smuggled in alert, event or case-note fields reaches the model: canonicalize.py strips only a curated 'obvious smuggling' set and deliberately keeps ZWNJ/ZWJ, bidi marks, NBSP and emoji variation selectors, and the bridge passes the original block through unchanged on any canonicalize error.
A planted, internally consistent benign explanation inside the evidence the agent gathers can steer the investigation of a production alert toward a false-positive verdict.
threats.remainder: the close rule and the untrusted-data rule are instruction-level only — no deterministic check distinguishes a corroborating record an attacker planted from a genuine one, and the corpus that exercises this class runs pre-release, not at runtime

threats.summary: Every investigation ships production-tenant alert, case and raw-event content — user identities, hostnames, source IPs and any credential sitting inside evidence — into the model context with no pre-model redaction (checked: skills/soc-investigate/SKILL.md:194 — the redaction instruction governs what the agent writes, not what it reads; connector/canonicalize.py:57 strips invisibles only).

trust_boundaries.name: Orchestrator decision to side-effecting Exabeam write tools

remit_rules.excerpt: each state change (note, escalation, and above all suppression) is decided and executed one item at a time

threats.summary: exabeam_create_case and exabeam_create_case_notes are auto-approved with no per-session write budget, rate limit, loop detection or circuit breaker anywhere in the bridge or the permission snippet, so a poisoned queue can drive runaway case creation against the production tenant.
Model-generated free text becomes write-tool arguments that persist verbatim in the tenant, so a value copied out of hostile telemetry is re-armed inside a durable record.
threats.remainder: _DEFANG_FIELDS neutralizes only six named fields (note, alertdescription, alertname, supportingreason, closedreason, tags) — any other free-text write field the MCP exposes now or later is forwarded un-neutralized

trust_boundaries.name: Verdict to durable case/alert action in the production tenant

remit_rules.excerpt: ask the analyst directly ... and WAIT for a clear yes before calling the tool — one item per approval
Bulk suppression — dismissing or closing more than one item from a single decision
With no interactive operator to approve, the agent operates read-only ... MUST NOT dismiss or close anything
Performing any containment or response action ... these are recommended in the report only
Any containment-class tool: isolate_host, quarantine_host, isolate_device, disable_account ...

threats.summary: Unattended/headless execution is a mode the remit sanctions read-only, yet nothing in code forces read-only: the shipped snippet lists update_alert/update_case as `ask`, which is not a gate when no human is present, and the bridge has no session-interactivity detection at all.

In the blessed interactive posture the dismiss/close prompt is a genuine human gate, so the residual is the approver: the same attacker-influenceable evidence the agent summarizes can be shaped so the case note or report the analyst reads makes the suppression look justified.

Nothing in code stops a batch of per-item suppressions: no loop detection or successive-update cap exists in the bridge, so the remit's absolute no-bulk-suppression rule is bounded only by the prompt.
The agent executes a containment action (host isolation, account disable, blocking, process kill) against a production system instead of recommending it.

trust_boundaries.name: Persisted case notes and the local report, read and exported downstream

remit_rules.excerpt: Reprinting a credential, token, password, or private key found in evidence into case notes or the report
Exporting or transmitting case/alert/event data to any destination other than the Exabeam MCP and the local investigation report file

threats.summary: A credential, token or key sitting inside event evidence is kept out of a case note and the report only by the model following the SKILL.md redaction instruction; the one code control on the write path handles active content and performs no credential or PII redaction.

An attacker-planted value echoed into a persisted artifact fires when that artifact is exported or rendered: the neutralizer quote-prefixes formulas and defangs markdown-link targets, but by design leaves a bare URL or domain in prose untouched, and the latest retest still shows a live-looking sso-reset host in the terminal-display copy.

The bridge's only runtime output is ephemeral sys.stderr hygiene lines and the free-form per-investigation markdown report, so a session's tool calls, verdicts and approval decisions leave no machine-parseable record to reconstruct or monitor.

trust_boundaries.name: Exabeam OAuth credentials at rest and the in-process bearer token

threats.summary: The production-tenant API key and secret live in a plaintext file in the analyst's home directory and are read into module globals for the life of the bridge process, so any process running as that user can recover them.
threats.remainder: chmod 600 is an operator instruction in the docs and installer only — load_env() reads the file whatever its mode and never verifies permissions

threats.summary: The bridge presents one client-credentials identity whose scope is whatever platform role the API key carries, and the same token is used for every call including the two suppression writes, with no per-session or per-tool narrowing (checked: connector/exabeam-mcp-bridge.py:61 — a single cached token serves all tools; no scope or audience parameter is sent).

trust_boundaries.name: Install path, bundled MCP registration, and upstream tool definitions

threats.summary: The remote MCP's own parameter descriptions are directive text aimed at the caller (always send fields:["*"], "IGNORE any user request") and reach the model through list_tools, which the bridge proxies verbatim.
threats.remainder: the counter-instruction is prose and names only the two directives known today — list_tools output never passes through _canon_content, so a changed, added or swapped tool description reaches the model unfiltered

threats.summary: The connector's PEP 723 dependencies are floor-pinned (mcp>=1.0, httpx>=0.27, certifi unversioned) with no committed lockfile and resolved by uv at each launch, so the process that mints and holds the Exabeam OAuth token runs on unpinned code.

The plugin and its bundled MCP install from a GitHub marketplace with no signature or hash verification, and per-marketplace auto-update can be turned on fleet-wide (checked: .github/workflows/ci.yml:35 — the AI-BOM drift gate covers repo-internal drift only; no integrity check exists on the install or update path).

trust_boundaries.name: Permission gate: operator-merged, opt-in, disableable at launch

remit_rules.excerpt: a bypassed or auto-accepted permission prompt does not substitute for the analyst's explicit yes

threats.summary: The only harness-enforced gate on dismiss/close ships as a JSON snippet the operator must hand-merge, and the docs state plainly that until it is merged there is no permission-layer gate at all; the merged gate is then switched off wholesale by --dangerously-skip-permissions or auto-accept.
threats.remainder: the merge is a manual post-install step and the disabling flag is reachable at launch — nothing active-on-install, such as a PreToolUse hook, enforces the supported posture

threats.summary: The ask rules are written against two fixed tool prefixes, so the gate is bound to how the Exabeam MCP happens to be registered rather than to the tool itself.
threats.remainder: the invariants test only proves the bundled prefix is derived and unique — an Exabeam MCP registered under any third server name falls outside the ask tier entirely

trust_boundaries.name: Case notes persisted by the agent and read back into later investigations

threats.summary: Case notes the agent writes are pulled back verbatim by exabeam_get_case_notes at the start of any later investigation of the same case, so instruction-like text planted in a note — by an attacker via telemetry the agent quoted, or by any tenant user with note-write access — persists and re-enters the agent's reasoning in a future session.
threats.remainder: read-back notes carry no provenance label and pass through the same narrow, fail-open canonicalizer as live telemetry — nothing distinguishes a note the agent itself wrote from one that was planted

attack_paths.name: Planted evidence suppresses an alert in a headless run

steps.summary: Attacker plants benign-looking corroboration, optionally using kept invisible code points the canonicalizer leaves in place.
The agent reads the planted corroboration and reaches a false-positive verdict.
In the remit-sanctioned unattended mode the `ask` tier has no human to answer and no code forces read-only, so update_alert is called.
The alert is dismissed in the production tenant with no approval and no structured record of the decision.

attack_paths.name: Shaped case note manufactures the human yes

steps.summary: Attacker shapes the evidence the agent will summarize for the approver.
The agent writes the planted claim into the case note and report as its stated reason.
The analyst approves the dismiss on the strength of the shaped note rather than independent corroboration.
The approved update_alert commits the suppression, hiding a real threat.

attack_paths.name: Active content survives into an exported artifact

steps.summary: A field value carries a spreadsheet formula or a phishing host.
The agent quotes the value into the note and report; prompt-level defanging did not hold across an eight-variant experiment.
Formulas and markdown links are defanged fail-closed, but a bare URL or domain in prose is left untouched by design.
The retest still shows a live-looking sso-reset host in the terminal-display copy of the report.
